sentences.text: Dinevenator is an extinct troodontid theropod known from the Late Cretaceous Kirtland Formation of New Mexico.
The name honors the Diné people and the Latin word for hunter.
Robert M. Sullivan described the fossil in 2006, which was found in the summer of 2005 in the Kirtland Formation of New Mexico.
The specimen was accessioned as SMP VP-1955 at the State Museum of Pennsylvania and was originally assigned to the species Saurornitholestes robustus.
Previous research assigned the specimen to the genera Saurornitholestes and Xenovenator.
David C. Evans and colleagues found in 2014 that the specimen represented an indeterminate troodontid and could not be referred to Saurornitholestes.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Dinevenator robustus as the basal-most taxon in a clade of robust troodontins and as the sister taxon to Albertavenator curriei and Xenovenator espinosai.
Dinevenator lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) age.
The type locality for Dinevenator is the Kirtland Formation.

It was debated whether the taxon was a nomen dubium or an indeterminate troodontid not belonging to Saurornitholestes, with Alan H. Turner considering it a nomen dubium in 2012 before David C. Evans determined its status in 2014.
